component.name: Kick the Fly
component.summary: Kick a live simulation of a real fruit fly brain

description.p: A kick-the-buddy game whose buddy runs on the MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome: all 166,700 neurons are simulated live while you poke, swat and feed the fly in a first-person 3D room.

Play mode has challenges built on real experiments. Lab mode adds a validation dashboard that shows which published fly behaviors this simulation reproduces (and which it doesn't), repeated trials with statistics, data export and YAML protocol files that also run headless.

screenshot.caption: The 3D room with the live brain panel

description.p: The GPU by default in the game and a GPU-drawn brain view; a profiler overlay; activation and knockout screens and a read-only failure autopsy in the Lab; opt-in real neuron shapes; Puppeteer mode, lesion battles and a contraption builder; a fly's-eye view; opt-in brain sonification; a hopping frog and animated predators. The simulation is unchanged. Every new feature is tagged connectome, game rule or model prediction.

The Neurodex, a kill cam and a Neuron of the Day; a Lab toolkit (split-GAL4 lines, thermogenetics, a virtual patch clamp, simulated calcium imaging, pharmacology); opt-in microphone and streamer mode; predators, weather and a kitchen arena; a fly arcade (tournaments and racing, in-game points only); network science, sleep deprivation and sensitivity analysis; classic behavior rigs with pre-registered assays; guided mini-papers; a What's New screen. Every new behavior is tagged connectome, game rule or model prediction.
The 2.13.0 features (tool loadouts, a fruit tool, a self-test, a bug report that sends nothing, a first-launch tutorial) with a test fix; 2.13.0 itself was never published with files.

Tool loadouts: a hotbar of your chosen tools with presets, an editor and a tool wheel; a fruit tool; a self-test and a bug report that shows exactly what it contains and sends nothing; a first-launch tutorial.
The decoy female is visible in the 3D game, can be picked up, thrown and removed, and is kept in save states; a live readout of the neurons she drives; a visible cVA puff.
A cVA pheromone tool and a decoy female; the OpenGL backend runs many flies together (16 in real time); headless replay files; a language setting; real-science cards off by default.
Courtship song, aggression, a thermo arena and a day/night cycle; more validation tests; neuron search and a path tracer in the brain view; gamepad support; faster learning on the OpenGL backend.
Fixes a crash when a second sugar pile, alcohol drop or bomb was used up.
The fly now looks like a fruit fly instead of a bee: big red eyes, a pale tan body and dark-tipped abdomen with bands only on top.
Faster simulation with optional Numba or GPU backends (from source), bigger swarms, a video recorder, ten neurons drawn from their real reconstructed shapes, and fixes for spawning extra flies.
The blowtorch and the spray cans fire from the tool in your hand, and the laser's key shows as "=".
The AppImage opens the 3D game on current distributions again instead of falling back to 2D.

Two outdoor arenas: an open field with wind and sun, and an orchard where the fly feeds from fruit that regrows. Lab tools that test how robust the results are to the connectome itself (synapse threshold, sign flips, critical path, inhibition block), NWB export, and a second, negative E-PG compass test with wind.
Settings menu, Play and Lab modes, challenges, slow motion and save states, native Wayland, a validation suite, repeated trials with statistics, data export and headless protocol runs.
